stops.name: Mineral King Drill Site
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4102 waypoint, on Mt. Sharp bedrock beside the Gediz Vallis channel, with a view of the upper Gediz Vallis ridge. The rover stayed parked here while it drilled "Mineral King", its 40th drill hole, on sols 4107 to 4111. This stop is a proposed astronaut target at a real rover waypoint, not a surveyed sample site.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view, taken while the rover was parked here. Curiosity Mastcam (right) on sol 4107 (25 February 2024, 01:57:05 UTC): the "Mineral King" drill hole and its pile of tailings. Sol 4107 has no separate waypoint; it falls between the sol 4102 and sol 4128 waypoints, which are 5.8 m apart.
stops.why: Look at a drill hole in Mt. Sharp bedrock at the edge of Gediz Vallis, to compare the bedrock with the debris inside the channel.

stops.name: Sulfur Crystal Field
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4200 waypoint at Whitebark Pass in the Gediz Vallis channel. On 30 May 2024 (sol 4200) the rover drove over a stone and crushed it, revealing yellow crystals that its arm instrument showed were elemental (pure) sulfur, a first for Mars. Many similar white stones lie in the field around it. The rover drilled the nearby "Mammoth Lakes" rock from here in June 2024. How the sulfur formed is still an open question. This stop is a proposed astronaut target at a real rover waypoint.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view, taken while the rover was parked here. PIA26309: Curiosity Mastcam on sol 4208 (7 June 2024). Yellow crystals of elemental sulfur inside "Convict Lake", the rock the rover crushed on 30 May; the fragments are about 13 cm across. Colour adjusted to Earth-like lighting. Sol 4208 has no separate waypoint; it falls between the sol 4200 and sol 4210 waypoints, which are 0.8 m apart.
stops.why: Photograph the first pure sulfur crystals ever found on Mars, and the field of white sulfur stones around them.

stops.name: Kings Canyon Drill Site
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4255 waypoint on the floor of the Gediz Vallis channel. The rover stayed here until sol 4282 and drilled the "Kings Canyon" block on sol 4263 (3 August 2024), just before its 12th landing anniversary, then delivered the sample to CheMin and SAM. This stop is a proposed astronaut target at a real rover waypoint.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view, taken while the rover was parked here. Curiosity Mastcam (right) on sol 4263 (3 August 2024, 07:56:55 UTC): the "Kings Canyon" drill hole. Sol 4263 has no separate waypoint; it falls between the sol 4255 and sol 4282 waypoints, which are 1.6 m apart.
stops.why: Sample a block on the channel floor to learn what the Gediz Vallis flows carried down from higher up Mt. Sharp.

stops.name: Gediz Vallis Panorama
stops.description: Curiosity's sol 4350 waypoint on the western edge of Gediz Vallis, where the rover drove west out of the channel toward the boxwork. From here the crew can document the channel, the rocky ground it crossed, and the buttes on either side. This stop is a proposed astronaut viewpoint at a real rover waypoint.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. PIA26471: Curiosity Mastcam panorama on sol 4352 (2 November 2024), made of two mosaics (171 and 169 images) taken around midday while heading west away from Gediz Vallis. The butte on the left is "Texoli", on the right "Kukenán". Colour adjusted to Earth-like lighting. Sol 4352 has no separate waypoint; it falls between the sol 4350 and 4353 waypoints, which are 19.1 m apart.
stops.why: Climb onto the western edge and photograph the whole channel, with the buttes Texoli and Kukenán, before heading back.
